newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums unmoved by frigid weather.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums unmoved by frigid weather.

text.p: NWE gas oil premiums were largely unmoved by continuing cold weather on Monday, showing steady to lower levels in holiday-affected business in contrast to gains in futures inspired by the frigid conditions, traders said.

German physical demand stimulated by plummeting weekend temperatures enlivened barge activity but failed to arouse cargoes, partly due to modest buying interest and partly because many traders remain on leave, traders added.
Benchmark Jan IPE futures rose $6 to $223 a tonne on the colder weather sweeping across northern and southern Europe.

Premiums for heating oil barges were around Jan IPE +$1/1.75 for January 1-15 delivery, around Friday's levels and $1 higher than Christmas Eve. A parcel of German winter specification went for Jan IPE +$5 fob Amsterdam for delivery January 1-5. Low sulphur diesel barges traded at Jan IPE +$11/12 fob Flushing.
In cargoes, a Russian was done at Jan +$2.25 for delivery January 1-5, around 25 cents down. Low sulphur diesel was done at Jan IPE +$8.75 and +$9, over $1 lower.
Arbs from Europe to the United States are closed but heating oil remains offered from the U.S. Gulf to northwest Europe.
